[title] Survey Results Summary statistics Quantiles and boxplots Python/Colab Outlook Example 8: Comparing two distributions
[body] Recall the surface roughness distributions from two samples:
[body] Questions
[body] • Which sample has the larger standard deviation? • What are the implications?
[body] Prof. Oke (UMass Amherst) CEE 260/MIE 273 M1b: Summarizing Data September 10, 2026 8 / 16

FIGURE: [description of the image, not printed words] A plot has horizontal axis labelled “RMS (mm/m²)” with values 0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, and vertical axis labelled “Occurrence (%)” with values 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. Light and dark vertical bars extend across the range. A black curve rises from near 0, peaks near 50 at about 15%, then declines toward 250. Text beside the plot reads “Typical smooth road” with σₐ RMS = 20, μₐ RMS = 40, Mₐ RMS = 30, Rₐ RMS = 0:100, and “Typical rough road” with σₐ RMS = 60, μₐ RMS = 110, Mₐ RMS = 70, Rₐ RMS = 20:250.

novice.takeaway: The typical rough-road sample has the larger standard deviation (60 versus 20), so its surface-roughness values are more spread out than the smooth-road sample’s.
questions: What do the RMS and subscripted measures mean?
What practical effects follow from greater roughness variation?
novice.inferred_claim: A larger standard deviation indicates the rough-road sample has more variable surface roughness.

peer.takeaway: The rough-road sample has the larger standard deviation (60 versus 20), indicating its surface-roughness values are much more dispersed than the smooth-road sample’s.
questions: What do Mₐ RMS and Rₐ RMS represent?
peer.inferred_claim: Standard deviation distinguishes the substantially greater variability of rough-road surface roughness.

expert.takeaway: The rough-road sample has the larger RMS standard deviation (60 versus 20), reflecting much greater spread and a higher central roughness than the smooth-road sample.
expert.inferred_claim: Standard deviation distinguishes the substantially greater variability of rough-road roughness.
